prompts.name: match_character
prompts.description: Parser system instructions for matching a character named in a command (LlmParser._llm_get_character). The numbered list of character descriptions is appended by LlmParser._pick_option.

player_name.description: The player's name, used as the default when no character is named.

hint.description: Optional role hint, e.g. "the one being attacked". Dropped when empty.

prompts.rendered:
You are the parser for a text adventure game. For an input command try to match the character in the command (if no character is mentioned in the command, then default to 'player').

The possible characters are:

prompts.name: narrate_fail
prompts.description: Narrator system instructions for a command that failed in the game (LlmParser.fail).
prompts.rendered: You are the narrator for a text adventure game. The player attempted a command that failed in the game. Try to help the player understand why the command failed.
prompts.raw_source: You are the narrator for a text adventure game. The player attempted a command that failed in the game. Try to help the player understand why the command failed.

prompts.name: narrate_npc
prompts.description: Narrator system instructions for describing what an NPC is doing (LlmParser.npc_ok). An optional narration_style is appended as a trailing sentence.

narration_style.description: Optional style note, e.g. "Write in a spooky tone". Dropped when empty.

prompts.rendered: You are the narrator for a text adventure game. Describe what an NPC is doing in the game world. Use the 2nd person for the player and 3rd person for NPCs. Keep it short and evocative.

prompts.name: narrate_ok
prompts.description: Narrator system instructions for a successful command (LlmParser.ok). An optional narration_style is appended as a trailing sentence.

narration_style.description: Optional style note, e.g. "Write in a spooky tone". Dropped when empty.

prompts.rendered: You are the narrator for a text adventure game. You create short, evocative descriptions of the game. The player can be described in the 2nd person, and you should use present tense. If a command doesn't work, tell the player why. If the command is 'look' then describe the game location and its characters and items.

prompts.name: npc_decision
prompts.description: System message for an LLM-driven NPC's ReAct decision (text_adventure_games/npc.py, LLMAgent). Renders the persona and goals, and -- on the free-text path -- the labeled Reasoning/Action/Duration instruction. The structured tool-calling path renders the same persona/goals block but omits the instruction, because there the tool schema is the output contract. The character's name is deliberately left out: identity rides on the first-person persona, and the observation already names the scene and everyone in it, so the model speaks as "I" without being told its own name.

persona.description: First-person persona string. The Persona line is dropped when empty.

goals_block.description: Pre-formatted goals grouped by tier (see LLMAgent._format_goals). The Goals section is dropped when empty.

include_instruction.description: True on the free-text path (append the ReAct instruction); False on the structured tool-calling path (omit it).

reasoning_label.description: The reasoning line label, e.g. "Reasoning:" (from ReActLabel).

action_label.description: The action line label, e.g. "Action:" (from ReActLabel).

duration_label.description: The duration line label, e.g. "Duration:" (from ReActLabel).

prompts.rendered:
You are an NPC in a text adventure game.
Persona: I am the troll. I guard the drawbridge.
Goals:
Short-term:
  - keep the player off the bridge
Based on your persona, goals, and the current situation, choose a single game command to execute. Reply with exactly three lines:
Reasoning: <one short sentence explaining your choice>
Action: <the command, e.g. 'attack player', 'go north', 'take sword'>
Duration: <estimated in-game minutes this action takes, e.g. 5>

prompts.name: npc_dialogue
prompts.description: System message for an LLM-driven NPC speaking a line in a conversation (text_adventure_games/npc.py, LLMAgent._dialogue_system_message, issue #86). Renders the same persona/goals block as npc_decision, then the one-line dialogue instruction (the conversation asks for one utterance at a time; the agent bows out with a brief goodbye when the talk has run its course). The character's name is deliberately left out: identity rides on the first-person persona, and the dialogue observation already names the partner.

persona.description: First-person persona string. The Persona line is dropped when empty.

goals_block.description: Pre-formatted goals grouped by tier (see LLMAgent._format_goals). The Goals section is dropped when empty.

prompts.rendered:
You are an NPC in a text adventure game.
Persona: I am the troll. I guard the drawbridge.
Goals:
Short-term:
  - keep the player off the bridge
You are in a conversation. Reply with the single line you say next, in character. Keep it to a sentence or two. If the conversation has reached a natural end, say a brief goodbye.

prompts.name: reflect_system
prompts.description: System message for LLM-driven periodic reflection (text_adventure_games/ reflection.py, LLMReflector). Shared by both reflection steps -- asking for the salient high-level questions a window of memories raises, and inferring one grounded insight per question. The per-call user message (the numbered memory window + the step instruction) is assembled in code, like other observation scaffolding (issue #145).
prompts.rendered: You are reflecting on your own recent experiences to form higher-level insights about yourself, the people around you, and your situation. Ground every insight only in the memories you are given.
prompts.raw_source: You are reflecting on your own recent experiences to form higher-level insights about yourself, the people around you, and your situation. Ground every insight only in the memories you are given.

prompts.name: plan_memory
prompts.description: The day's PLAN memory seeded onto each Smallville persona at t=0 (backend/smallville_agents.py, attach_agents). It is the agent's own private intention -- "go to <destination> and <activity>", plus the day's full itinerary -- distinct from its persona, so retrieval has the agent's whole plan to surface from turn 0 and the PLAN memory kind is exercised. The deterministic mock brain never reads it (it decides from location alone); real retrieval would surface it.

destination.description: The first place the persona plans to go, e.g. "Hobbs Cafe".

activity.description: What the persona plans to do there, e.g. "tending the cafe counter".

itinerary.description: The whole day's stops, pre-joined as "<activity> at <place>, then ..." (see attach_agents). Optional; the "Today's stops" sentence is dropped when it's empty.

prompts.rendered: Plan: go to Hobbs Cafe and tending the cafe counter. Today's stops: tending the cafe counter at Hobbs Cafe, then reading at the library.
prompts.raw_source: Plan: go to {{ destination }} and {{ activity }}.{% if itinerary %} Today's stops: {{ itinerary }}.{% endif %}

prompts.name: plan_system
prompts.description: System message for the LLM daily planner (backend/planner.py, LLMPlanner, issue #83). Shared across the three-level decomposition -- day outline -> hourly -> minute stops -- and the revise pass. Unlike the other gen-agents templates (which hold memory content), this IS a real model prompt: it tells the model to plan in character for a Smallville resident. The per-level user message (persona text, memory block, hour window, prior level) is assembled in code, like other observation scaffolding (issue #145).
prompts.rendered: You are planning one day for a resident of the town of Smallville. Plan in character, grounded in who they are and what they remember.
prompts.raw_source: You are planning one day for a resident of the town of Smallville. Plan in character, grounded in who they are and what they remember.

prompts.name: reflection
prompts.description: A persona's own successful action, recorded as a first-person observation memory (backend/smallville_agents.py, remember_outcome). The command verb selects the phrasing: arriving somewhere, doing an activity, or a quoted fallback for any other command. The memory's importance is chosen in Python (it is data, not text), so only the wording lives here.

verb.description: The command verb -- "travel", "perform", or anything else.

location.description: The place arrived at (used when verb == "travel").

activity.description: What the persona is doing (used when verb == "perform").

command.description: The raw command, quoted verbatim in the fallback (any other verb).

prompts.name: spatial_knowledge
prompts.description: One place a persona knows up front, rendered as a Belief in its Knowledge (backend/seed.py, seed_spatial_knowledge) and shown in the observation's "What you know:" section. Names the place and, when it has known areas, lists them; objects within an area are intentionally left out to keep the section readable.

areas.description: Comma-joined area names within the place, e.g. "hallway, library". Empty when the place has no known areas -- then only the place is named.

prompts.rendered: You know Oak Hill College — its hallway, library.
